gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Keychron's own low-profile keyboards accept only low-profile parts, and only some of them: K3 Max hot-swap applies 'for RGB Backlight Hot-Swappable Version only' with Gateron low-profile MX-style switches, and Keychron's low-profile LSA keycap set 'is not compatible with the Keychron K1 versions 1 to 5, K1 SE, K3, K5, K5 SE, and K7'. A full-height board like the Q1 Max instead takes ordinary full-size switches (Gateron Jupiter, sold by Keychron at $13.99 a set).
standout_why: Both saved ChatGPT chats ran with an empty search and got no result pages, so there were no rival pages to compare against. The only nearby claim is ChatGPT's own table row 'Customization: More limited' for low-profile, with no source. It names no switch or keycap standard and no generation or variant exclusions. It also recommends the K3 Max without saying that hot-swap depends on which version you buy.
decides: This supports the low-profile pick for laptop-style typists, with one condition: a low-profile board ties you to low-profile switches and keycaps, and in Keychron's case to particular versions. If the shopper wants to change switches on a K3 Max, they must buy the RGB hot-swappable version. Low-profile keycaps from Keychron's current sets will not fit the original K3, K1 v1–5, K5 or K7. Shoppers who want to swap keycaps and switches freely should buy a full-height board (Q1 Max class). This matches ChatGPT's 'enthusiasts → standard' line, but gives the actual reason.
